definition: Outer radius of a plasma filament is the geometric radius of the outer circular boundary of the annular cross-section representing a current-carrying plasma filament. It marks the external boundary of the conducting annular region.
documentation:
Outer radius of a plasma filament is the geometric radius of the outer circular boundary of the annular cross-section representing a current-carrying plasma filament. It marks the external boundary of the conducting annular region; material outside this boundary is not part of that annular filament cross-section.

For the outer circular boundary in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the outer radius $r_\mathrm{outer}$ is the distance from the filament cross-section center $(R_c, Z_c)$ to any point $(R, Z)$ on that boundary:

$$
r_\mathrm{outer} = \sqrt{(R - R_c)^2 + (Z - Z_c)^2}
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, $(R_c, Z_c)$ is the center of the annular cross-section, and $(R, Z)$ lies on the outer circular boundary.

The quantity applies only to the outer boundary of an annular plasma-filament cross-section and is a single geometric radius for that boundary, not an average over the conducting region. It is the outer member of radius of a plasma filament, paired with the [inner radius](name:inner_radius_of_plasma_filament) $r_\mathrm{inner}$; by definition $0 \le r_\mathrm{inner} \le r_\mathrm{outer}$, and the current-carrying cross-section occupies the annular region between the two radii. For the same annular geometry, the area of a plasma filament $A$ satisfies $A = \pi(r_\mathrm{outer}^2 - r_\mathrm{inner}^2)$, where $A$ is the area of the annular plasma-filament cross-section and $\pi$ is the circle constant. This quantity excludes the major radius of the filament center about the toroidal symmetry axis and rectangular cross-section dimensions such as [plasma filament width](name:plasma_filament_width) and [height of a plasma filament](name:height_of_plasma_filament).

definition: Poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis is the signed equilibrium flux through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle at that location.
documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis is the signed [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux) through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle at that location. It is the magnetic-axis value of the equilibrium [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) function.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, its defining relation is

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a} = \Phi_{\mathrm{p}}(R_a,Z_a) = 2\pi \int_0^{R_a} B_Z(R',Z_a)\,R'\,dR'
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a}$ is the magnetic-axis poloidal flux, $\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux function, $R_a$ and $Z_a$ are the magnetic-axis coordinates, $R'$ is the major-radius integration variable, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component.

This value includes both externally generated and plasma-current-generated flux; it is not an external-source-only contribution. It is an unnormalized flux value and need not vanish at the magnetic axis.

Together with the [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), denoted by $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b}$, it defines the normalized poloidal-flux coordinate $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},N} = (\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a})/(\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b}-\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a})$. This coordinate is zero at the magnetic axis and one at the plasma boundary, provided the two reference flux values differ. These physical reference endpoints apply even when the flux-coordinate interval under consideration does not extend to the axis or boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the net vertical magnetic field threading the integration disk is directed toward increasing $Z$.

The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged. Where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}) = 0$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal magnetic field; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the O-point inside the nested closed flux surfaces.

definition:
Normalized toroidal beta is the whole-plasma toroidal pressure beta rescaled by minor radius and signed reference toroidal field relative to plasma current. It is dimensionless (unit 1), with defining normalization beta_N = 100 * beta_tor * a[m] * B0[T] / Ip[MA], where a is the positive plasma minor radius, B0 is the nonzero signed reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field and Ip is the nonzero signed net toroidal plasma current; their numerical values are taken in metres, teslas and megaamperes, respectively. The underlying beta_tor = 2*mu_0*

/B0^2 uses vacuum permeability mu_0 and the whole-plasma volume average

of total perpendicular plasma pressure, including the represented thermal and nonthermal contributions. For the equilibrium-reconstruction variant, the pressure is determined by an equilibrium reconstruction code without changing the normalization. The signed ratio B0/Ip is preserved. The quantity is a global scalar evaluated at each equilibrium time slice; the bound profile-derived and summary representations are one-dimensional arrays.
documentation:
Normalized toroidal beta is the conventional current-and-geometry rescaling of the whole-plasma toroidal pressure beta. Its defining normalization is $\beta_{\mathrm{N}}=100\,\beta_{\mathrm{tor}}\,a[\mathrm{m}]\,B_0[\mathrm{T}]/I_p[\mathrm{MA}]$. Here $\beta_{\mathrm{N}}$ is normalized toroidal beta, $\beta_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the dimensionless [toroidal beta](name:toroidal_beta), $a$ is plasma minor radius, $B_0$ is the signed reference vacuum toroidal magnetic field and $I_p$ is the signed net toroidal plasma current. The bracketed units specify the numerical values used in this conventional normalization.

The underlying toroidal pressure ratio, before that rescaling, obeys $$\beta = \frac{2\mu_0 \langle p\rangle}{B^2}$$ with $\beta=\beta_{\mathrm{tor}}$, $B=B_0$, $\mu_0$ vacuum permeability and $\langle p\rangle$ the whole-plasma volume average of the total perpendicular pressure $p$ used to form the toroidal beta. This pressure-ratio equation defines the operand $\beta_{\mathrm{tor}}$; it is not the defining equation of $\beta_{\mathrm{N}}$.

The pressure input includes the thermal and nonthermal contributions represented by the total-pressure input. A pressure estimate obtained from equilibrium reconstruction changes that pressure input rather than the normalization. Restricting the pressure input to thermal pressure defines the separately named [normalized toroidal thermal beta](name:normalized_toroidal_thermal_beta).

The normalization requires positive minor radius and nonzero reference field and plasma current. It preserves the signed ratio $B_0/I_p$ without silently replacing either by its magnitude. For nonnegative underlying toroidal beta, the sign of the normalized value follows that ratio. The normalized quantity differs from unnormalized toroidal beta by the explicit factor of 100 and the stated size, field and current factors.

definition: Toroidal total current density is the net conventional charge flux per unit area around the symmetry axis, formed by algebraically summing all included current contributions. It is the signed local projection onto increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical height, and is measured in A.m^-2. It is represented on general-grid subsets for various time slices in edge-plasma, plasma-profile, and wall-physics data, with one scalar value per element in the grid subset, stored as a one-dimensional array; the edge-plasma and plasma-profile arrays are indexed from 1 to N. For edge-plasma and plasma-profile data, the timebase must be a subset of the ggd_fast timebase if the ggd_fast array of structures is used.
documentation:
Toroidal total current density is the signed local projection of the net [current density](name:current_density) onto the toroidal direction. It combines all included contributions before or after projection onto that same direction.

The projection and aggregation are defined by:

$$
j_\phi = \hat{\phi}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}} = \sum_k \hat{\phi}\cdot\mathbf{j}_k
$$

where $j_\phi$ is the toroidal total current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total current-density vector, $\mathbf{j}_k$ is an included current-density contribution, and $k$ labels those contributions. The unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The total is an algebraic sum, not a sum of magnitudes, and does not select a particular species, charge state, or current-generation mechanism. The quantity is local, with no restriction to a particular plasma region; it is neither a current-density magnitude nor a flux-surface average or spatially integrated current.

This quantity specializes [total current density](name:total_current_density) by fixing its common signed projection to the toroidal direction. The adjacent [radial total current density](name:radial_total_current_density) instead projects the same net charge-flux density onto the outward major-radius direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the net conventional charge transport is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, counterclockwise when viewed from above along the negative vertical direction.

definition: Alpha angle specifying the first inclination of an oblique poloidal-field-coil conductor-element cross-section, measured from the outward major-radius direction. In the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, it is the scalar α = atan2(a₁·Ẑ, a₁·R̂), where a₁ points along the first cross-sectional axis, R̂ points outward in major radius, and Ẑ points upward. The angle is quadrant-resolved and positive from the outward major-radius direction toward increasing vertical height. It is an individual-element shape parameter, not an average over the coil, and is expressed in radians.
documentation:
Alpha angle $\alpha$ specifies the inclination of the first cross-sectional axis at a coil conductor element. It applies to the oblique trapezoidal or parallelogram cross-sectional geometry of an active poloidal-field coil.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the angle is defined by

$$
\alpha = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left(\mathbf{a}_1\cdot\hat{Z},\,\mathbf{a}_1\cdot\hat{R}\right)
$$

where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The vector $\mathbf{a}_1$ points along the first cross-sectional axis; $\hat{R}$ and $\hat{Z}$ are the outward major-radius and upward unit vectors, respectively. The function $\operatorname{atan2}$ returns the quadrant-resolved angle from the radial and vertical projections.

This is an individual-element shape parameter, not an average over the coil. The [tilt angle of the coil conductor element](name:tilt_angle_of_coil_conductor_element) specifies the separate second inclination of the same cross-section.

Sign convention: Positive when the first cross-sectional axis rotates from the outward major-radius direction toward increasing vertical height.

definition: Electrical resistivity of the material assigned to a mobile plasma-facing component unit, relating local electric field to current density and governing its conductive electromagnetic response.
documentation:
Electrical resistivity is the material property that determines the electric field required to sustain conduction in a mobile plasma-facing component unit. It governs induced-current and eddy-current response within that unit.

For an isotropic material, the local constitutive relation is

$$
\mathbf{E} = \rho\,\mathbf{J}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector, $\rho$ is the electrical resistivity, and $\mathbf{J}$ is the conventional current-density vector.

This quantity applies to the material of one mobile plasma-facing component unit and is not summed over multiple units or converted into a lumped resistance. It is a local material property, distinct from the effective resistivity of a broader passive conducting structure or [wall material](name:resistivity_of_wall_material). When geometry is included, it contributes to a lumped [passive-loop resistance](name:resistance_of_passive_loop), which also depends on current-path length and cross-sectional geometry.

definition: Effective turn count of a passive loop element is the signed number of equivalent windings assigned to a passive axisymmetric conducting loop element for electromagnetic coupling in calculating magnetic fields of the coil/loop. It weights the passive-loop current contribution and may be fractional for equivalent or homogenized loop elements. Positive means current is counter-clockwise when seen from above. It is a dimensionless scalar with unit 1.
documentation:
Effective turn count of a passive loop element is the signed number of equivalent windings assigned to a passive conducting loop element for electromagnetic coupling. It may be fractional when the represented conductor is an equivalent or homogenized passive-loop element rather than a literal winding. Positive means current is counter-clockwise when seen from above.

The signed current-turn source strength represented by the passive loop element is defined by:

$$
\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{loop}} = N_{\mathrm{eff}} I_{\mathrm{loop}}
$$

where $\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{loop}}$ is the signed current-turn source strength of the passive loop element, $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective turn count of the passive loop element, and $I_{\mathrm{loop}}$ is the [current of the passive loop](name:current_of_passive_loop).

This quantity applies to the represented passive-loop element as one electromagnetic circuit contribution. Each loop is comprised of a number of cross-section elements described individually. It has no implicit aggregation over multiple passive loops; if several represented windings or conductor pieces are collapsed into one loop element, their net orientation and coupling are represented by the single algebraic value of $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$.

It is distinct from the [current of the passive loop](name:current_of_passive_loop), which is multiplied by $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$, and from the [area of the passive loop](name:area_of_passive_loop), which describes conductor cross section. It is not a turn count for magnetic probes, coil conductor elements, toroidal-field coils, or magnetic field-line winding.
enclosing_statements: Each loop is comprised of a number of cross-section elements described individually

Passive axisymmetric conductor description in the form of non-connected loops; any connected loops are expressed as active coil circuits with no power supply attached. Array of passive conductor loop structures describing axisymmetric conducting elements not actively driven by a power supply. Each loop is characterized by its geometry, resistance, resistivity, and time-resolved induced current from inductive coupling.

definition: Flux-surface-averaged magnetic-field magnitude is the mean strength of the total equilibrium field, with the local magnitude taken before averaging. The local magnitude is the Euclidean norm of the total field vector. At each equilibrium time slice, it is a one-dimensional radial profile as a function of poloidal magnetic flux, obtained on each closed nested magnetic flux surface as ⟨B⟩ = (∮ B dS/|∇ψ|)/(∮ dS/|∇ψ|), where ψ is the poloidal magnetic-flux label and dS is the surface area element. Thus the average is weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient and normalized by the integral of that weight over the surface. It is positive for a nonvanishing equilibrium field, irrespective of the sign convention for the magnetic-field direction, and is expressed in T.
documentation:
Flux-surface-averaged magnetic-field magnitude is the mean strength of the total equilibrium [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field) on each closed nested magnetic flux surface.

Its defining relation is

$$
\langle B\rangle = \oint B\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \,/\, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $B$ is the local total [magnetic-field magnitude](name:magnetic_field_magnitude), $\langle B\rangle$ is its flux-surface average, $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic-flux label, $\nabla\psi$ is the gradient of that label, and $dS$ is the area element of the closed surface over which both integrals are taken.

All equilibrium magnetic-field components contribute to the local magnitude before averaging. This quantity is not a selected field component, a pointwise field strength, or the magnitude of a surface-averaged field vector. It is positive for a nonvanishing equilibrium field.

The [flux-surface-averaged squared magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude) instead averages the square of the local field strength. That second moment is not the square of this mean unless the field strength is constant over the surface.

The flux-surface average is the average of a quantity over a closed magnetic flux surface, weighted by the inverse magnitude of the poloidal flux gradient.

The magnitude is the Euclidean norm of a vector quantity, or the modulus of a complex one.

definition: Signed rotation of a probing laser beam's linear-polarization orientation induced by crossing magnetized plasma, accumulated from plasma entry to exit along one beam path and expressed in rad. Positive rotation follows the right-hand rule about the beam-propagation direction relative to the incident polarization orientation. The value is obtained either by polarimetric measurement or by calculation from a reconstructed equilibrium along the same path. In the cold, weakly dispersive magnetoionic limit, the electron contribution is α = [e^3 λ^2/(8π^2 ε0 m_e^2 c^3)] ∫ n_e B_parallel dℓ, where λ is the vacuum probing wavelength, e is the elementary-charge magnitude, ε0 is the vacuum permittivity, m_e is the electron mass, c is the speed of light, and B_parallel is signed along beam propagation. The integral covers only the beam segment inside the plasma; rotation from external optics or calibration elements is excluded.
documentation: Faraday angle measures plasma-induced rotation of the polarization orientation, not polarization ellipticity, which describes the polarization ellipse's shape, nor the emission polarization orientation measured by the motional Stark effect. It is an accumulated angle along a single probing-beam path, rather than a local rotation rate, a flux-surface average, or an average over channels. Polarimeter channels report this angle, and equilibrium reconstruction uses measured values as constraints and calculates corresponding values from the reconstructed state. Measured and reconstructed values represent the same physical quantity; their difference is a fit residual, not another definition of Faraday angle.
enclosing_statements: Set of faraday angles Set of Faraday angle measurements used as constraints in equilibrium reconstruction. Each entry stores measured, reconstructed, and residual values for the polarimetric rotation angle of a laser beam passing through magnetized plasma.

In case of equilibrium reconstruction under constraints, measurements used to constrain the equilibrium, reconstructed values and accuracy of the fit. The names of the child nodes correspond to the following definition: the solver aims at minimizing a cost function defined as : J=1/2*sum_i [ weight_i^2 (reconstructed_i - measured_i)^2 / sigma_i^2 ]. in which sigma_i is the standard deviation of the measurement error (to be found in the IDS of the measurement)
Set of equilibria at various time slices

Set of channels (lines-of-sight) Array of measurement channels (lines of sight) in a polarimeter diagnostic, each recording the initial polarization state, probing wavelength, and time-resolved Faraday rotation angle and ellipticity induced by the magnetized plasma.

definition: Electromotive-force contribution to the plasma loop voltage caused by changing externally generated poloidal magnetic flux, including flux linked through active coils and passive conducting structures. This global, zero-dimensional scalar is evaluated as V_ext(t) = −dΦ_ext(t)/dt, where Φ_ext(t) is the externally generated poloidal magnetic flux linked by the considered toroidal plasma circuit and t is time. It excludes resistive voltage drops and other non-inductive contributions. Its sign follows the COCOS ip_like convention: positive when the induced electromotive force has a positive line integral in the direction of increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. Its unit is V.
documentation:
This quantity is the inductive electromotive-force contribution to the plasma loop voltage produced by time-varying poloidal magnetic flux generated by active coil circuits and magnetically coupled passive conducting structures. It excludes resistive voltage drops and other non-inductive contributions.

The contribution is defined by Faraday's law:

$$
V_{\mathrm{ext}}(t) = -\frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the externally generated poloidal magnetic flux linked by the considered toroidal plasma circuit and $t$ is time. It contributes to the total [loop voltage at the plasma boundary](name:loop_voltage_at_plasma_boundary); currents in passive conductors are represented by the linked-flux response of structures such as those described by [current of passive structure](name:current_of_passive_structure).

Sign convention: Positive when the induced electromotive force has a positive line integral in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
name: external_loop_voltage

definition: Complex E-minus contribution of a coherent electromagnetic-wave electric field, transverse to the static magnetic field and retaining the amplitude and phase of its right-hand circular polarization.
documentation:
The right-hand circularly polarized wave electric field is the E-minus polarization contribution of the complex [wave electric field](name:wave_electric_field), perpendicular to the local static magnetic field. It retains the local amplitude and phase of that circular-polarization contribution.

Its vector contribution is defined by the circular-basis projection

$$
\widetilde{\mathbf E}_{-}=\widetilde E_{-}\mathbf e_{-}=\mathbf e_{-}\left(\mathbf e_{-}^{*}\cdot\widetilde{\mathbf E}_{\mathrm{wave}}\right)
$$

where $\widetilde{\mathbf E}_{-}$ is the right-hand circularly polarized vector contribution, $\widetilde E_{-}$ is its complex coefficient, $\widetilde{\mathbf E}_{\mathrm{wave}}$ is the wave-electric-field phasor, and the asterisk denotes complex conjugation. The circular basis vector is $\mathbf e_{-}=(\hat{\mathbf e}_1+i\hat{\mathbf e}_2)/\sqrt{2}$, where $i$ is the imaginary unit. The real unit vectors form a local right-handed orthonormal frame $(\hat{\mathbf e}_1,\hat{\mathbf e}_2,\hat{\mathbf b})$, with $\hat{\mathbf b}$ pointing along the static magnetic field and the first two directions perpendicular to it.

With temporal dependence $e^{-i\omega t}$, where $\omega$ is the wave angular frequency and $t$ is time, this polarization rotates opposite to positive-ion gyromotion. The complementary [left-hand circularly polarized wave electric field](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field) co-rotates with positive ions. Handedness is defined relative to the static magnetic field, not the wave-propagation direction.

This quantity includes only the right-hand transverse wave contribution; it excludes the parallel wave component and non-wave electric fields. It is local and is not restricted to a beam or ray path. The full complex contribution is distinct from its amplitude representation, which removes the coefficient's complex phase, and from its real and [imaginary quadratures](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part), which separately retain phase-referenced parts of the same phasor.

This component drives ion cyclotron resonance heating (ICRH) and is key to wave-particle coupling.

definition: Geometric rate of change of the cumulative volume enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface as its signed poloidal flux coordinate varies. It is evaluated separately at each equilibrium time slice as a one-dimensional radial profile in poloidal flux, with time held fixed during differentiation. Its unit is Wb^-1.m^3.
documentation:
This quantity is the geometric derivative of the cumulative volume enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface with respect to its signed poloidal magnetic-flux coordinate.

It is defined by

$$
\frac{dV}{d\psi}=\frac{d}{d\psi}V(\psi)
$$

where $V(\psi)$ is the volume enclosed by the flux surface labeled by $\psi$, $\psi$ is the signed poloidal magnetic-flux coordinate, and $d/d\psi$ denotes differentiation with respect to that coordinate.

The quantity applies separately to each nested closed flux surface. The underlying volume is cumulative from the magnetic axis to the selected surface, so this derivative describes the change in enclosed volume along the flux coordinate rather than a local volume density, a shell volume, or a plasma-population-weighted quantity.

It is the derivative of [volume enclosed by a flux surface](name:volume_of_flux_surface); integrating it between two flux-coordinate values gives the difference between the corresponding enclosed volumes. It is distinct from the derivative with respect to the toroidal flux coordinate, which is represented by [derivative of volume with respect to toroidal flux coordinate](name:derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate).

Sign convention: Positive when the enclosed volume increases in the direction of increasing signed poloidal magnetic flux $\psi$.

Set of equilibria at various time slices

definition: Geometric radial derivative dV/dψ of the cumulative volume V enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface with respect to its signed, dimensionful poloidal magnetic-flux coordinate ψ, with other coordinates held fixed. It is obtained by differentiating the enclosed-volume profile V(ψ), and is positive when volume increases with increasing ψ. The unit is Wb^-1.m^3.
documentation: This equilibrium quantity is specified on the one-dimensional poloidal-flux grid for each time slice. The volume is cumulative from the magnetic axis to the selected flux surface, so dV/dψ describes the change in enclosed volume per change in poloidal magnetic flux, not a shell volume or a local volume density. It differs from the enclosed-volume derivative with respect to the toroidal-flux coordinate by the differentiation coordinate, and from the poloidal cross-sectional-area derivative by the geometric quantity differentiated. Integrating dV/dψ between two poloidal-flux values gives the difference in their enclosed volumes.

definition: Wave phase of the wave beam is the angular argument of the probing-wave envelope; when referenced to launch, it is the envelope phase offset from the launch phase.
documentation:
The wave phase is the angular argument of the complex probing-wave envelope at the wave-beam locus. It is defined relative to a phase origin; when the origin is the launch phase, the value is a signed phase difference rather than an absolute phase with a universal zero.

For a launch-referenced value, the phase difference is:

$$
\varphi = \varphi_{\mathrm{env}} - \varphi_{\mathrm{launch}} \pmod{2\pi}
$$

where $\varphi$ is the launch-referenced phase difference, represented by difference of wave phase and launched wave phase of the wave beam; $\varphi_{\mathrm{env}}$ is the envelope phase at the wave-beam locus; and $\varphi_{\mathrm{launch}}$ is the launched wave phase. The phases use the same phase convention, and $2\pi$ is one full phase revolution.

This quantity is the envelope phase, not the carrier oscillation phase. Values differing by an integer number of full revolutions represent the same phase; an unwrapped phase selects a continuous branch, and fringe-jump correction changes that representation without changing the phase modulo one revolution.

Sign convention: Positive when the envelope phase at the wave-beam locus advances counterclockwise relative to the launch phase, using the positive-time-exponent phasor convention.

definition: Radial shift of ablated pellet material from its ablation location to its final deposition location attributable to E×B drift. It is obtained as the normalized toroidal flux coordinate at deposition minus that at ablation: Δρ_tor,N = ρ_tor,N,dep − ρ_tor,N,abl. The displacement is dimensionless, with unit 1.
documentation: Each value describes the deposition-relative-to-ablation shift of material released at the corresponding point along the pellet path, rather than a displacement integrated along that path. Only the contribution attributed to E×B drift is included. Radial position is represented by the normalized toroidal flux coordinate; the quantity is therefore neither toroidal motion nor a geometric distance, an absolute deposition coordinate, or a drift velocity. It describes redistribution of ablated material, not the injection motion of the pellet.

definition: Loop voltage at the plasma boundary is the electromotive force around a closed toroidal loop that provides the inductive drive for ohmic plasma current. The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface. The voltage is obtained as the electric-field circulation around that loop, including inductive contributions from both external sources and plasma currents, and is expressed in V. Positive voltage drives positive ohmic current flowing counterclockwise viewed from above, along increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical height.
documentation:
Loop voltage at plasma boundary

The voltage is defined by the electric-field circulation:

$$
V_{\mathrm{loop}} = \oint_C \mathbf{E}\cdot d\mathbf{l}
$$

where $V_{\mathrm{loop}}$ is the boundary loop voltage, $C$ is the closed toroidal loop at the plasma boundary, $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric field, and $d\mathbf{l}$ is the directed line element along the loop.

The total includes inductive contributions from both external sources and plasma currents. In contrast, [external loop voltage](name:external_loop_voltage) denotes only the contribution from changing externally generated linked magnetic flux. The inductive electric field provides the drive for [current due to ohmic current drive](name:current_due_to_ohmic_current_drive); the loop voltage is not an electrostatic potential difference between two points.

Sign convention: Positive when the electric-field circulation is directed along increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counterclockwise viewed from above) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi = \psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux; $\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

definition: Dimensionless minor-radius label of a magnetic flux surface, obtained by normalizing its major-radius half-width to a specified positive reference length.
documentation:
This quantity is the dimensionless minor-radius label assigned to a magnetic flux surface from its radial extent in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{minor}} = \frac{R_{\max}-R_{\min}}{2L_{\mathrm{ref}}}
$$

where $R_{\max}$ and $R_{\min}$ are the maximum and minimum major-radius coordinates of the surface, each in m, and $L_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the specified positive reference length in m.

The label is a geometric normalization of the surface half-width; it is not a magnetic-flux normalization and therefore is distinct from the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). Its numerical value depends on the chosen reference length.
enclosing_statements: Flux surface characteristics

source_descriptions: Normalised minor radius of the flux surface of interest = 1/2 * (max(R) - min(R))/L_ref

definition: Poloidal beta compares volume-averaged total perpendicular plasma pressure with an effective poloidal magnetic-pressure scale set by net plasma current and plasma geometry.
documentation: Poloidal beta compares the volume-averaged plasma pressure with a current-based poloidal magnetic-pressure scale. Its source normalization is $\beta_p=4\int_V p\,dV/(R_0\mu_0 I_p^2)$. Here $p$ is the pressure supplied by the plasma or equilibrium representation, $V$ is the evaluation volume, $R_0$ is the reference major radius, $\mu_0$ is vacuum permeability and $I_p$ is the plasma current used by that normalization. The global value uses the plasma volume; a profile reports the source's specified evaluation volume. Writing $\langle p\rangle_V=V^{-1}\int_Vp\,dV$, the same quantity obeys the canonical beta relation $$\beta = \frac{2\mu_0 \langle p\rangle}{B^2}$$ with $\beta=\beta_p$, $\langle p\rangle=\langle p\rangle_V$ and $B=B_{p,\mathrm{ref}}$. The effective reference field satisfies $B_{p,\mathrm{ref}}^2=\frac{\mu_0^2I_p^2R_0}{2V}$. The reference field is an effective current-based scale rather than a pointwise poloidal field. The normalization requires nonzero $I_p$ and positive evaluation volume. It is neither an average of local pressure-to-field ratios nor an unnormalized pressure. Unlike [toroidal beta](name:toroidal_beta), it uses the current-based poloidal scale.

definition: Dimensionless shape parameter of the plasma-boundary poloidal cross-section, obtained as the arithmetic mean of its upper and lower triangularities: δ = [(R_geo − R_u)/a + (R_geo − R_l)/a]/2. Here R_geo is the major radius of the geometric axis, R_u and R_l are the major radii of the upper and lower vertical extrema, and a is the boundary minor radius, using right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) coordinates. Inward offsets are positive and outward offsets are negative. The unit is 1.
documentation: Plasma-boundary triangularity describes the normalized inward radial displacement of the boundary’s vertical extrema, combining both extrema into one shape parameter. The plasma boundary denotes the last closed magnetic flux surface bounding the confined plasma. Unlike upper_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary and lower_triangularity_of_plasma_boundary, which each use only one vertical extremum, this quantity is their arithmetic mean and can therefore conceal differences between the upper and lower shapes. It differs from triangularity_of_flux_surface by describing the plasma boundary rather than an individual nested flux surface, and from elongation or squareness by measuring extremal radial displacement rather than vertical-to-radial extent or corner shape.

definition: Apparent surface temperature is the temperature inferred from infrared radiance at the exposed material boundary of a plasma-facing component, at a specified surface point and time. It refers to the apparent surface material state, not to an area aggregate or regional extremum.
documentation:
Apparent surface temperature is the temperature inferred from infrared radiance at the exposed boundary of a plasma-facing component. It is a local scalar assigned to a specified material surface point and time, representing the apparent state of the surface material rather than the temperature of the adjacent plasma, sheath, neutral gas, or radiation field.

For an extended exposed surface, the unqualified quantity denotes the local point value at each surface point, not an area average, integral, percentile, or extremum. Region-level aggregates require distinct standard names; the maximum over a specified exposed surface region is [maximum_surface_temperature](name:maximum_surface_temperature). [temperature_at_wall](name:temperature_at_wall) is the corresponding boundary-locus temperature when the wall is the defining locus.

definition: Poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis is the signed equilibrium flux through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle at that location. In the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle and Z is vertical height, it is obtained as Φ_p,a(t) = Φ_p(R_a(t), Z_a(t), t) = 2π ∫_0^{R_a(t)} B_Z(R′, Z_a(t), t) R′ dR′, where R_a and Z_a are the magnetic-axis coordinates and B_Z is the vertical magnetic-field component. It includes both externally generated and plasma-current-generated flux, is unnormalized, and need not vanish at the magnetic axis. Its sign is positive when the net vertical magnetic field threading the disk is directed toward increasing Z. It is a zero-dimensional scalar at each time slice and may be represented as a one-dimensional function of time. Together with the plasma-boundary flux Φ_p,b, it supplies the axis reference for the normalization (Φ_p − Φ_p,a)/(Φ_p,b − Φ_p,a), provided the reference values differ, even when the radial grid does not extend to the axis or boundary. The unit is Wb.
documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the magnetic axis is the signed [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux) through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle at that location. It is the magnetic-axis value of the equilibrium [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) function.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, its defining relation is

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a} = \Phi_{\mathrm{p}}(R_a,Z_a) = 2\pi \int_0^{R_a} B_Z(R',Z_a)\,R'\,dR'
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a}$ is the magnetic-axis poloidal flux, $\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux function, $R_a$ and $Z_a$ are the magnetic-axis coordinates, $R'$ is the major-radius integration variable, and $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component.

This value includes both externally generated and plasma-current-generated flux; it is not an external-source-only contribution. It is an unnormalized flux value and need not vanish at the magnetic axis.

Together with the [poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary), denoted by $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b}$, it defines the normalized poloidal-flux coordinate $\Phi_{\mathrm{p},N} = (\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}-\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a})/(\Phi_{\mathrm{p},b}-\Phi_{\mathrm{p},a})$. This coordinate is zero at the magnetic axis and one at the plasma boundary, provided the two reference flux values differ. These physical reference endpoints apply even when the flux-coordinate interval under consideration does not extend to the axis or boundary.

Sign convention: Positive when the net vertical magnetic field threading the integration disk is directed toward increasing $Z$.

The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged. Where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}) = 0$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal magnetic field; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the O-point inside the nested closed flux surfaces.

definition: Thermodynamic temperature associated with a selected thermocouple sensor attached to a tokamak structural component.
documentation:
This quantity is the absolute thermodynamic temperature associated with one selected sensor member, represented by the thermal state at its thermocouple junction. It characterizes the local thermal condition of the attached structural component at the sensor location.

For a system in thermodynamic equilibrium, temperature is defined by

$$
T = \left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial S}\right)_{V,N}
$$

where $T$ is thermodynamic temperature, $U$ is internal energy, $S$ is entropy, $V$ is volume, and $N$ is the amount of material or particle number held fixed in the derivative.

The quantity applies to the selected sensor member individually and is not a sum, average, or other aggregation over the sensor set. It denotes the sensor or junction thermal state associated with a structural component, not the temperature of a flowing coolant or of an entire plant connection.

It is distinct from [coolant temperature at inlet](name:coolant_temperature_at_inlet), which describes fluid entering a cooling system. Object-specific quantities such as [temperature of a coil conductor](name:temperature_of_coil_conductor) and [temperature of a neutron detector](name:temperature_of_neutron_detector) apply the same thermodynamic concept to explicitly named hardware rather than to the generic sensor locus.

source_descriptions: Temperature measured by a thermocouple

definition: Signed major-radius separation from the separatrix after mapping a measurement position along its flux surface to the outboard midplane, with positive values in the scrape-off layer.
documentation:
This quantity is the signed major-radius offset between a measurement position mapped along its magnetic flux surface to the outboard midplane and the separatrix at that locus.

The defining relation is

$$
\Delta R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}} = R_{\mathrm{mapped}} - R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}
$$

where $\Delta R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}$ is the signed separation, $R_{\mathrm{mapped}}$ is the major radius of the mapped measurement position, and $R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}$ is the major radius of the separatrix intersection at the outboard midplane. Both radii are coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The mapping preserves the magnetic flux label of the original measurement position. The result is a difference of major radii, not the [radial coordinate assigned to a flux surface](name:radial_coordinate_of_flux_surface), an unmapped local separation, or the shortest distance normal to the separatrix. It vanishes on the separatrix and is negative on the confined-plasma side.

Sign convention: Positive when the mapped measurement position has a larger major radius than the separatrix at the outboard midplane, corresponding to the scrape-off-layer side.

The low-field-side equatorial midplane: the point of maximum major radius on the flux surface in question. For a value at the separatrix intersection use outboard_midplane_separatrix. Where $R = \max_{S} R,\quad R > R_{\mathrm{axis}}$, $S$ is the magnetic flux surface the point lies on; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is major radius of the magnetic axis.

definition: Poloidal magnetic flux evaluated at the magnetic axis of an axisymmetric equilibrium, expressed in Wb. In the right-handed cylindrical frame (R, φ, Z), it is Φ_p,a = Φ_p(R_a, Z_a) = 2π∫₀^{R_a} B_Z(R′, Z_a) R′ dR′, the signed flux through the horizontal disk bounded by the toroidal circle at the magnetic-axis coordinates (R_a, Z_a). The sign is positive for net flux directed toward increasing Z. This unnormalized equilibrium value includes both external-source and plasma-current contributions and need not be zero. Its locus is the magnetic axis, where the poloidal magnetic field vanishes at the O-point inside nested closed flux surfaces, rather than the plasma boundary or another evaluation position.
documentation: The magnetic axis is the closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged. This quantity is the value of the poloidal magnetic-flux function there, not a toroidal flux, a magnetic-field component, or a weighted external-only flux. Together with the poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary, Φ_p,b, it supplies the physical reference values for the dimensionless poloidal-flux fraction (Φ_p − Φ_p,a)/(Φ_p,b − Φ_p,a), provided the denominator is nonzero. That fraction is zero at the axis and one at the boundary; the reference values remain applicable when a radial grid does not reach either endpoint. The quantity recorded here is the dimensional axis flux itself, not the normalized fraction.

definition: Instantaneous injection rate of ethylene (C2H4) gas into the plasma vessel, expressed as equivalent electrons per second with each molecule counted as 16 equivalent electrons.
documentation:
Ethylene (C2H4) is a two-carbon, four-hydrogen molecule used as a gaseous source of both carbon and hydrogen in plasma fueling and wall-conditioning experiments. The source rate is the instantaneous equivalent-electron delivery rate to the plasma vessel, where each molecule is assigned 16 equivalent electrons based on the total atomic electron inventory of the molecular formula.

The equivalent-electron rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq}$ relates to the molecular injection rate $\dot{N}_\mathrm{C_2H_4}$ by

$$
\dot{N}_\mathrm{eq} = 16\,\dot{N}_\mathrm{C_2H_4}
$$

where the factor $16 = 2Z_\mathrm{C} + 4Z_\mathrm{H}$, with $Z_\mathrm{C} = 6$ the carbon atomic number and $Z_\mathrm{H} = 1$ the hydrogen atomic number.

The injection rate is inferred from valve conductance calibrations and upstream pressure measurements. Its time-integral gives the [accumulated ethylene count](name:accumulated_ethylene_count), which tracks the total equivalent-electron inventory delivered since plasma breakdown. Related molecular and atomic injection rates include [silane_source_rate](name:silane_source_rate) for SiH4 and [hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) for atomic hydrogen delivery.

Sign convention: Positive when ethylene gas flows from the injection system into the plasma vessel.
name: ethylene_source_rate

definition: Signed vertical position of the plasma-current centroid, obtained by weighting the toroidal current distribution by height in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, integrating over the poloidal plasma cross-section and normalizing by total plasma current at each equilibrium time slice; expressed in m.
documentation:
The vertical coordinate of the plasma-current center is the current-density-weighted centroid height of the plasma current distribution in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

$$
Z_{\mathrm{c}} = \frac{\int_{\mathcal{A}} Z\,j_{\phi}(R,Z)\,dA}{\int_{\mathcal{A}} j_{\phi}(R,Z)\,dA}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{c}}$ and $Z$ are vertical coordinates in m, $R$ is major radius in m, $j_{\phi}$ is toroidal current density in A m$^{-2}$, $dA$ is differential poloidal cross-sectional area in m$^{2}$, and $\mathcal{A}$ is the region carrying plasma current. The current-weighted center is distinct from the geometric axis; its radial counterpart is the [radial coordinate of the current center](name:radial_coordinate_of_current_center).

Sign convention: Positive when the plasma-current centroid lies in the $+Z$ direction from the coordinate origin.

definition: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of all gas species introduced by injection during the plasma prefill phase, summed over species.
documentation:
This quantity is the total gas inventory accumulated during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron count and summed over all injected species. It represents the integrated amount introduced before plasma breakdown, rather than an instantaneous injection rate.

The accumulated equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = \sum_s \int_{t_0}^{\min(t,t_1)} \dot{N}_{s,\mathrm{eq}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $s$ indexes injected gas species, $\dot{N}_{s,\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron injection rate of species $s$, $t_0$ and $t_1$ delimit the prefill phase, and $t$ is the evaluation time. The sum includes all species; a species-specific quantity such as [accumulated hydrogen prefill count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count) is a component of this total. The quantity is distinct from the instantaneous injection rate and from inventories restricted to one species, while [accumulated prefill gas count](name:accumulated_prefill_gas_count) denotes the near-equivalent total inventory.
name: accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count

definition: Orientation indicator equal to the sign of the toroidal magnetic-field component on a flux surface in local gyrokinetic geometry. It is the dimensionless scalar s_phi = B_phi/|B_phi|, where B_phi = B · phi_hat is the equilibrium magnetic-field component along increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, with R the major radius and Z the vertical height. It equals +1 for a component directed toward increasing toroidal angle and -1 for the opposite direction, and is undefined when B_phi vanishes. Unit: 1.
documentation:
The toroidal magnetic-field sign specifies whether the equilibrium toroidal field component on a flux surface is directed along or opposite increasing toroidal angle in local gyrokinetic geometry.

For a nonzero toroidal magnetic-field component, the orientation indicator is defined by

$$
s_\phi = \operatorname{sgn}(B_\phi) = \frac{B_\phi}{|B_\phi|}
$$

where $s_\phi$ is the orientation indicator, $B_\phi$ is the toroidal magnetic-field component, and $\operatorname{sgn}$ is the sign function. The component is $B_\phi = \mathbf{B}\cdot\hat{\phi}$, where $\mathbf{B}$ is the equilibrium magnetic field and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

As the toroidal member of [parity](name:parity), this quantity retains only field orientation and takes the values $+1$ or $-1$; the two-valued indicator is undefined when the toroidal component vanishes. It does not specify field strength, plasma-current direction, or the even or odd symmetry of a gyrokinetic perturbation.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal magnetic-field component points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

definition: Effective turn count of a passive loop is the signed number of equivalent windings assigned to a passive conducting loop for electromagnetic coupling. It weights the passive-loop current contribution and may be fractional for equivalent or homogenized loop elements.
documentation:
Effective turn count of a passive loop is the signed number of equivalent windings assigned to a passive conducting loop for electromagnetic coupling. It may be fractional when the represented conductor is an equivalent or homogenized passive-loop element rather than a literal winding.

The signed current-turn source strength represented by the passive loop is defined by:

$$
\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{loop}} = N_{\mathrm{eff}} I_{\mathrm{loop}}
$$

where $\mathcal{I}_{\mathrm{loop}}$ is the signed current-turn source strength of the passive loop, $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective turn count of the passive loop, and $I_{\mathrm{loop}}$ is the [current of the passive loop](name:current_of_passive_loop).

This quantity applies to the represented passive loop or passive-loop element as one electromagnetic circuit contribution. It has no implicit aggregation over multiple passive loops; if several represented windings or conductor pieces are collapsed into one loop element, their net orientation and coupling are represented by the single algebraic value of $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$.

It is distinct from the [current of the passive loop](name:current_of_passive_loop), which is multiplied by $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$, and from the [area of the passive loop](name:area_of_passive_loop), which describes conductor cross section. It is not a turn count for magnetic probes, coil conductor elements, toroidal-field coils, or magnetic field-line winding.

definition: Vertical coordinate of a plasma filament geometry point, giving its signed height from the zero-height plane in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. The specified point is the reference point from which the alpha and beta angles are defined for an oblique parallelogram cross-section, or the second endpoint of the central segment for a thick-line rectangular cross-section. The coordinate is a scalar measured in m.
documentation:
Vertical coordinate of a plasma filament geometry point specifies its signed height in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis.

The coordinate is defined by:

$$
Z = \mathbf{x}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is the position vector of the specified point relative to the coordinate origin and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along the positive symmetry-axis direction.

The specified point is the reference point for an oblique cross-section or the second endpoint of the central segment for a thick-line cross-section. The quantity applies to one filament geometry point, not an average over filaments or a coordinate of the plasma boundary. Unlike the [vertical outline of a plasma filament](name:vertical_outline_of_plasma_filament), it specifies a point location rather than a contour.

Sign convention: Positive when the specified point lies on the positive-$Z$ side of the zero-height plane.

definition: Major-radius coordinate of the plasma-current centroid in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame at each equilibrium time slice, obtained by normalizing the toroidal-current first moment over the poloidal plasma cross-section by total plasma current, expressed in m.
documentation:
The radial coordinate of the current center is the major-radius location of the centroid of the toroidal plasma-current distribution. It identifies a current-weighted position and is distinct from the geometric centroid or the magnetic axis.

The coordinate is defined by the toroidal-current first moment:

$$
R_c = \frac{\displaystyle\int_{D_p} R\,j_\phi\,dS}{I_p}
$$

where $R_c$ is the major-radius coordinate of the current center, $R$ is the major-radius coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $j_\phi$ is the toroidal component of the plasma [current density](name:current_density), $dS$ is an element of poloidal cross-sectional area, $D_p$ is the plasma current-carrying poloidal cross-section, and $I_p$ is the total toroidal plasma current, equal to the corresponding integral of $j_\phi$ over $D_p$.

The quantity applies to the full plasma-current distribution and uses a current-weighted first-moment aggregation over the poloidal cross-section. It excludes weighting by particle density, pressure, magnetic-field strength, or geometric area alone; the resulting position is therefore not a generic geometric center.

This quantity is a locus-specific instance of the general [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate), evaluated at the current center. Its vertical counterpart, [vertical coordinate of the current center](name:vertical_coordinate_of_current_center), supplies the corresponding vertical position needed to locate the current centroid in the cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

definition: Area enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface in a poloidal plane at fixed toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, obtained at each equilibrium time slice by integrating dR dZ over the complete enclosed planar interior and expressed in m^2, defining the equilibrium plasma cross-sectional size at the plasma boundary.
documentation:
This quantity is the geometric area enclosed by the last closed magnetic flux surface (LCFS), which forms the plasma boundary, in a poloidal cross-section.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the enclosed area is defined by

$$
A_{\rm LCFS} = \iint_{\mathcal{S}_{\rm LCFS}} dR\,dZ
$$

where $A_{\rm LCFS}$ is the LCFS cross-sectional area, $\mathcal{S}_{\rm LCFS}$ is the region enclosed by the LCFS contour at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and $dR\,dZ$ is the poloidal-plane area element.

This is a global equilibrium quantity for the complete plasma-boundary contour. It is not a local surface element, a flux-surface average, or the area of a toroidal surface formed by revolving the contour.

It is the plasma-boundary specialization of [poloidal plane cross-sectional area of a flux surface](name:poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface), whose corresponding area is defined for an arbitrary closed magnetic flux surface; the LCFS is the outermost such surface enclosing the plasma.
enclosing_statements: 0D parameters of the equilibrium

source_descriptions: Area of the LCFS poloidal cross section

definition: Minimum gas flow is the smallest pressure-volume gas throughput that a gas injection valve can reliably deliver, defining the lower bound of its controllable range. Pressure-volume throughput is p_g dV_g/dt, where p_g is gas pressure at the flow boundary and dV_g/dt is the volumetric flow rate across that boundary; the unit is Pa.m^3.s^-1.
documentation:
Minimum gas flow is the lower reliable operating limit of the pressure-volume throughput delivered by a gas injection valve. It identifies the smallest controllable value of the aggregate gas stream throughput, rather than a molecular-species flow or particle-number rate.

The pressure-volume throughput represented by this quantity is defined as

$$
Q_g = p_g \frac{dV_g}{dt}
$$

where $Q_g$ is gas pressure-volume throughput, $p_g$ is gas pressure at the flow boundary, $V_g$ is the volume of gas crossing that boundary, and $t$ is time.

This quantity applies to the aggregate gas stream delivered through an injection system across a defined flow boundary. The stream is not restricted to a particular molecular species or charge state, and this quantity is distinct from mass flow and particle-number rate. Its defining distinction is the lower reliable operating bound, rather than an unrestricted instantaneous throughput.

The gas flow quantity defines the same pressure-volume throughput without imposing a lower-limit condition; minimum gas flow is its lower reliable operating bound. Conversely, [maximum gas flow](name:maximum_gas_flow) is the upper reliable operating bound, so the two quantities delimit the controllable range rather than represent different throughput definitions.
enclosing_statements: Set of valves connecting a gas bottle to pipes
name: lower_bound_gas_flow_of_valve
source_descriptions: Minimum flow rate of the valve

definition: Azimuthal coordinate of a point on a control surface about the machine symmetry axis, expressed in rad in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is defined by φ = atan2(y, x) modulo 2π, with zero set by the facility-defined reference direction and positive angles increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above along the +Z axis toward the origin. The source supplies these coordinates as the toroidal angle array on which the Fourier decomposition of the normal magnetic field is carried out.
documentation: This quantity locates control-surface points in the toroidal direction; it is not the toroidal angle of a launching position, outlet, diagnostic measurement position, or antenna strap. It is an angular coordinate rather than the control surface's major-radius or vertical coordinate, and it is not a magnetic-field component or an angular offset from a reference position. The source stores a one-dimensional array of these angles for the control-surface Fourier decomposition. Angles differing by an integer multiple of 2π identify the same toroidal direction.

definition: Toroidal magnetic field at the magnetic axis is the signed component of the total equilibrium magnetic field in the toroidal direction, including external-coil and plasma-current contributions. It is computed from the equilibrium reconstruction as the local projection B_axis · φ̂ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, positive in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, counterclockwise when viewed from above. The magnetic axis is the closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged, located at the poloidal-field O-point where B_p = 0. The value is neither a magnetic-field magnitude nor a flux-surface average. It is a scalar at each equilibrium time slice; the summary representations are one-dimensional arrays of local values. Its unit is T.
documentation:
Toroidal magnetic field at the magnetic axis is the signed toroidal projection of the total equilibrium [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field). It is evaluated locally at the magnetic axis.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the defining projection is:

$$
B_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}} = \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{axis}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $B_{\phi,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the toroidal magnetic field at the magnetic axis, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the total equilibrium magnetic-field vector at that locus, and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle.

The total field includes externally applied and plasma-current-generated contributions. The corresponding projection of the [vacuum magnetic field](name:vacuum_magnetic_field) excludes plasma-current contributions and is therefore a distinct quantity. This on-axis value is neither a magnetic-field magnitude nor a flux-surface average.

Sign convention: Positive when the magnetic field at the magnetic axis projects in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from above.

The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged. Where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}) = 0$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal magnetic field; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the O-point inside the nested closed flux surfaces.

definition: Signed major-radius separation from the separatrix after mapping a measurement position along its flux surface to the outboard midplane, with positive values in the scrape-off layer. The scalar is R_mapped - R_sep,mid, expressed in metres (m), with the mapping preserving the original magnetic flux label. Both radii are coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, where R is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, phi is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height. The outboard midplane is the point of maximum major radius on the flux surface in question, with R > R_axis, where R_axis is the major radius of the magnetic axis.
documentation:
This quantity is the signed major-radius offset between a measurement position mapped along its magnetic flux surface to the outboard midplane and the separatrix at that locus.

The defining relation is

$$
\Delta R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}} = R_{\mathrm{mapped}} - R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}
$$

where $\Delta R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}$ is the signed separation, $R_{\mathrm{mapped}}$ is the major radius of the mapped measurement position, and $R_{\mathrm{sep,mid}}$ is the major radius of the separatrix intersection at the outboard midplane. Both radii are coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The mapping preserves the magnetic flux label of the original measurement position. The result is a difference of major radii, not the [radial coordinate assigned to a flux surface](name:radial_coordinate_of_flux_surface), an unmapped local separation, or the shortest distance normal to the separatrix. It vanishes on the separatrix and is negative on the confined-plasma side.

Sign convention: Positive when the mapped measurement position has a larger major radius than the separatrix at the outboard midplane, corresponding to the scrape-off-layer side.

The low-field-side equatorial midplane: the point of maximum major radius on the flux surface in question. For a value at the separatrix intersection use outboard_midplane_separatrix. Where $R = \max_{S} R,\quad R > R_{\mathrm{axis}}$, $S$ is the magnetic flux surface the point lies on; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is major radius of the magnetic axis.

definition: Flux-surface-averaged collisional energy-transfer rate per unit volume to the co-passing part of a fast-particle distribution from one specified charge state of an ion species, in W.m^-3. The profile is evaluated using the co-passing part of the distribution. Positive values denote energy gain by that fast-particle population; negative values denote energy loss.
documentation: This quantity resolves the collisional power received by co-passing fast particles according to the interacting ion species and charge state. The co-passing restriction applies to the fast-particle distribution receiving the power, not to the interacting ion charge state, and the fast particles are not necessarily ions. Unlike the total co-passing fast-particle collisional power density, this quantity includes only the contribution associated with the specified ion charge state, without a sum over ion species or charge states. It differs from the corresponding thermal power density by describing power to the fast-particle population rather than to thermal ions. It is a flux-surface-averaged power per unit volume, not stored energy density or volume-integrated power; the sources do not specify a numerical evaluation method or an averaging weight.

definition: Net conventional electric current carried by charged particles into all divertor target surfaces, including signed electron and ion contributions.
documentation:
The total divertor current is the algebraic conventional current delivered by charged particles crossing the plasma-facing surfaces of the complete divertor assembly. It includes ion and electron contributions and excludes neutral-particle flux and displacement current.

The current is defined by

$$
I_{\mathrm{div}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA = \int_{S_{\mathrm{div}}} \sum_s q_s\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $I_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the total current in A, $S_{\mathrm{div}}$ is the union of divertor target surfaces, $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{ch}}$ is conventional charged-particle current density in A m$^{-2}$, $q_s$ is the signed charge of species $s$ in C, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_s$ is its particle flux density in m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$, and $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ points from the plasma toward the material.

This assembly-integrated quantity differs from [current at a divertor target](name:current_at_divertor_target), which applies to one target, and [current of a divertor tile](name:current_of_divertor_tile), which applies to an individual tile.

Sign convention: Positive when conventional charged-particle current flows from the plasma into the divertor material.
enclosing_statements: Set of divertors
name: current_of_divertor
source_descriptions: Total current incident on this divertor

definition: Signed toroidal magnetic flux through the poloidal cross-section enclosed by the selected plasma boundary, obtained as Phi_tor,b = integral over Omega_b of B_phi dA_RZ, where Omega_b is that cross-section and B_phi is the total toroidal magnetic-field component. In the right-handed cylindrical (R, phi, Z) frame, positive flux corresponds to field in the direction of increasing phi, counter-clockwise when viewed from above +Z. The flux includes externally imposed and plasma-poloidal-current contributions, without normalization or division by 2*pi. Its unit is Wb.
documentation: This scalar is the boundary value of toroidal magnetic flux, rather than its value on an arbitrary interior flux surface. The source records it at equilibrium/time_slice/boundary/phi for the selected boundary used by fixed-boundary codes, typically chosen at normalized poloidal flux of 99.x% of the separatrix value; the selected computational boundary therefore need not coincide exactly with the last closed magnetic flux surface. Unlike toroidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary_due_to_poloidal_current, it is not restricted to the plasma-current contribution. Unlike poloidal magnetic flux at the plasma boundary, it integrates the toroidal field through a poloidal cross-section, not the poloidal field through a horizontal disk.

definition: Electromotive-force contribution to the plasma loop voltage caused by changing externally generated poloidal magnetic flux, including flux linked through active coils and passive conducting structures.
documentation:
This quantity is the inductive electromotive-force contribution to the plasma loop voltage produced by time-varying poloidal magnetic flux generated by active coil circuits and magnetically coupled passive conducting structures. It excludes resistive voltage drops and other non-inductive contributions.

The contribution is defined by Faraday's law:

$$
V_{\mathrm{ext}}(t) = -\frac{d\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(t)}{dt}
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the externally generated poloidal magnetic flux linked by the considered toroidal plasma circuit and $t$ is time. It contributes to the total [loop voltage at the plasma boundary](name:loop_voltage_at_plasma_boundary); currents in passive conductors are represented by the linked-flux response of structures such as those described by [current of passive structure](name:current_of_passive_structure).

Sign convention: Positive when the induced electromotive force has a positive line integral in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.
name: external_loop_voltage

definition: Dimensionless amplitude c_k of a basis term in an angular expansion f(theta) = sum_k c_k b_k(theta) representing the cross-sectional shape of a magnetic flux surface. The coefficient is specified relative to the chosen shape function, angular parameterization, basis and its normalization; no particular harmonic or trigonometric parity is prescribed. The flux surface comprises points sharing a magnetic-flux label in a nested-flux-surface configuration, with psi(R, Z) = const where psi is poloidal magnetic flux. Unit: 1.
documentation: This quantity describes an individual angular expansion term for a specified flux surface, rather than a surface average, an enclosed-volume integral or an overall geometric descriptor such as elongation or squareness. A collection of these scalar coefficients is indexed by expansion term, not by spatial direction. The sine coefficient of a flux surface is the specialization to sine terms; this general coefficient does not impose that restriction. Values depend on the chosen representation, so coefficients from different bases or normalization conventions are not necessarily directly comparable.

definition: Full vertical extent of the rectangular cross-section of a discrete plasma current-carrying filament element, measured along the machine’s vertical axis.
documentation:
This quantity is the full vertical dimension of the rectangular cross-section associated with one discrete plasma current-carrying filament. It is a geometric extent, not the filament current or its current density.

The height $H$ is defined by the difference between the upper and lower vertical coordinates:

$$
H = Z_{\mathrm{upper}} - Z_{\mathrm{lower}}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{upper}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{lower}}$ are the upper and lower coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $Z$ denoting vertical height and $\hat{Z}$ the vertical basis direction.

This quantity applies only to the vertical dimension of the rectangular filament cross-section. The horizontal full width is defined separately by [plasma filament width](name:plasma_filament_width), while the in-plane thickness is defined by thickness of plasma filament.

definition: Tritium prefill count is the amount of tritium introduced by gas injection before plasma breakdown, expressed as one equivalent electron per tritium atom.
documentation:
Tritium prefill count is the accumulated amount of neutral tritium introduced by gas injection during prefill before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. Each tritium atom contributes one equivalent electron; a neutral diatomic tritium molecule contributes two.

The equivalent-electron count is defined by

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{T,prefill}} = N_{\mathrm{T,prefill}} = \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{T,prefill}}$ is the tritium equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{T,prefill}}$ is the accumulated count of injected tritium atoms including molecular constituents, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is their introduction rate, $t$ is time, $t_0$ is the prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity counts injected tritium, not the retained or ionized tritium inventory. It excludes post-breakdown gas injection, wall recycling, neutral-beam fueling, and pellet fueling. The equivalent-electron convention is an accounting normalization based on neutral atomic composition, not an actual free-electron count.

It is the tritium contribution to the [total prefill gas count](name:accumulated_total_prefill_gas_equivalent_electron_count), which sums over all injected species. The [accumulated tritium count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_tritium_count_due_to_gas_injection) instead counts tritium introduced after plasma breakdown.
enclosing_statements: Tritium

Accumulated injected gas during the prefill in equivalent electrons Container grouping accumulated injected gas quantities during the plasma prefill phase, expressed in equivalent electrons, organized by gas species. Covers hydrogenic isotopes, noble gases, and impurity species.
name: accumulated_tritium_prefill_count
